items.title: Positive-gamma pin cage intact while the intraday tape rolls from one-way up to two-sided reversal risk under narrow breadth into the close
items.note: The dealer-gamma structure and the intraday tape have diverged into the pre-close window. SPY still sits in positive dealer gamma (signedNetGEX +$15.63B, spot 777.03 above the 771.18 flip, call wall 780 / put wall 770), a pinning, move-dampening cage that favors fades inside the 770/780 band. Yet the intraday tape has rolled over from the earlier one-way up-auction to a Reversal risk auction under Algo-controlled control (VWAP 776.92), even as market breadth stays narrow (heatmap 49.85% positive vs the 60% threshold, margin -10.15) against a bull-stacked bench (swing 20>50>200) and calm volatility (vol forecast 13.37%, throttle ×1.12). The tell is that the same positive-gamma pin that muffled downside now sits under a tape that has lost its directional conviction while participation remains thin — a suppressed-range, low-conviction drift rather than a broad advance. It is an emergent cross-tool divergence, not any single owner read: the pin cage keeps ranges tight, but the reversal-risk tape plus sub-half breadth argue against chasing strength, and the read flips to break-watch if spot loses the 771.18 flip.
items.method: Cross-tool divergence flag: take the options-structure and gamma-trading dealer-gamma sign together with spot-versus-flip position (pin vs break), then overlay the intraday-tape session type and the market-heatmap breadthPct-versus-threshold margin. Raise the pattern when dealer gamma is positive AND spot sits above the flip (pinning) AND breadth is below its 60% threshold AND the intraday tape has shifted away from a one-way trend to a reversal-risk or balanced session — flagging a gamma-caged, low-conviction range under narrow internals rather than a healthy trend. Invert to break-watch once spot falls below the flip (positive gamma lapses) or the tape re-establishes a one-way trend on broadening breadth.
